correctness.rationale: For any read sequence, the leftmost-subsequence embedding counts canonical separated-run-end and adjacent deletion masks; their exact algebra yields B_2=binom(R,2)+H-T. For consecutive ell-mers from an i.i.d. q-ary word, adjacent-read equality iff an ell+1-letter constant substring, giving exact pair probability q^(-ell-min(d,ell)). The H-T expectation cancels to p, yielding the stated finite mean. The centered constant-run sum is finite-dependent and has variance growth v>0; the quadratic remainder has second moment O(m^2), the local remainder O(m), proving both the Gaussian law and variance limit. Actual package verifier checked 294061 input words across 48 complete parameter grids by constructing all deletion outputs; exact rational means and local formula all agree. Finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Searches of public mathematical records and primary paper texts found no exact q-ary overlapping-window two-deletion mean plus Gaussian law. The general double-deletion pointwise run identity is explicitly treated as prior technique; novelty is the correlated sliding-window expectation and nondegenerate CLT with explicit overlap covariance. Xie–Chen treat code redundancy and fixed adapters, Chee et al. locally constrained sequence enumeration, Abbasian et al. mixed-error spheres, and the closest published binary variance and a previously accessible all-alphabet iid-word moment claim concern independent symbol inputs. This is best-knowledge originality only, with unindexed or not retrieved equivalences a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed formulation of the correlated-read ball-size central limit theorem may predate this work; absence of a search hit is not a mathematical proof of novelty.
The closest 2026 coding paper assumes protected adapters, so this unguarded theorem is not a direct result for its full operational channel; no such claim is made.

value.rationale: Unlike mere worst-case cardinality, the finite expectation and sharp nondegenerate fluctuation law measure typical ambiguity after two read deletions for every q,ell, including the quaternary DNA alphabet. Overlapping reads have nonzero covariances, and these induce the explicit positive correction v_q,ell to the leading variance coefficient. The exact cancellation of longer-run and period-two effects yields an economical all-length average formula. This motivated analytic benchmark is meaningful without a downstream rate theorem or broad channel performance guarantee.
